title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DARNELL'S MIC
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Darnell Pickett, a car wash manager in Shreveport, Louisiana.
Everybody at work says he's the funniest man in town.
But he had never told one joke to a room full of strangers.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN-UP SHEET
segments.quote: You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
segments.author: Eleanor Roosevelt
lines: His coworker Lupe taped a flyer to the vacuum station. Open mic, Tuesday, Red River Room.
Darnell sat in the parking lot and almost drove home.
Then he pictured his mom's fridge magnet, from Eleanor Roosevelt:
You must do the thing you think you cannot do.
He walked in and signed the list, before he could change his mind.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FIVE LONG MINUTES
segments.quote: Ever tried. Ever failed. No matter. Try again. Fail again. Fail better.
segments.author: Samuel Beckett
lines: He got one laugh in five minutes. It was when he sneezed.
By the door hung a poster from the Irish writer Samuel Beckett:
Ever tried. Ever failed. No matter. Try again. Fail again. Fail better.
So the next Tuesday, he was back. He failed again. But a little better.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE DAILY GRIND
segments.quote: Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
segments.author: Thomas Edison
lines: Darnell figured funny people are just born funny.
Miss Rhonda, a retired nurse and open mic regular, laughed and quoted Thomas Edison:
Genius is one percent inspiration and ninety-nine percent perspiration.
So he wrote jokes every morning before the wash opened, and fixed them at lunch between minivans.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE WRONG TARGET
segments.quote: Everything is funny, as long as it's happening to somebody else.
segments.author: Will Rogers
lines: His new jokes made fun of rude customers. The crowd just groaned.
Miss Rhonda quoted the old cowboy humorist Will Rogers:
Everything is funny, as long as it's happening to somebody else.
Then she said, so let it happen to you, honey.
So he told the truth. He runs a car wash and drives the dirtiest car in Louisiana.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BAD MONTH
segments.quote: Life is a tragedy when seen in close-up, but a comedy in long-shot.
segments.author: Charlie Chaplin
lines: Then his landlord sold the building, and Darnell moved back in with his mother. At thirty-four.
On her shelf sat an old Charlie Chaplin movie with a line on the box:
Life is a tragedy when seen in close-up, but a comedy in long-shot.
So he stepped back and wrote about it. Mom checks his curfew. Mom gives notes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE SHAKY WELDER
segments.quote: The best way to cheer yourself is to try to cheer somebody else up.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: At the big Friday showcase, Darnell's hands were shaking.
Next to him, a young welder named Kevin was shaking worse. His first night.
Darnell remembered a line from Mark Twain:
The best way to cheer yourself is to try to cheer somebody else up.
So he gave Kevin a pep talk and a mint. Then Darnell went up loose, and the room roared. Mom laughed loudest.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Sign up. Fail better. Do the work. Laugh at yourself. Step back. Cheer someone on.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Sign up anyway. Fail better. Do the work. Laugh at yourself. Step back. Cheer someone else on.
I tried stand-up once myself. They asked me to sit down.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
